prompt: A rotating platform lifts a robot to height $h = 5\sin\theta + 5$ metres as it spins. For $0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ$, at what angle $\theta$ is the robot HIGHEST? Give the angle in degrees.
hint: The height is biggest when $\sin\theta$ is biggest.

hints.text: The height is biggest when $\sin\theta$ is biggest.
The largest value sine can ever take is $1$. Which angle in one turn gives $\sin\theta = 1$?
$\sin 90^\circ = 1$, so the robot is highest at $\theta = 90^\circ$ (height $10$ m).

explanation: Only the $\sin\theta$ part changes; the $+5$ is fixed.
Sine tops out at $1$, and on the unit circle the height is $1$ only at the very top: $\theta = 90^\circ$.
There $h = 5 \times 1 + 5 = 10$ m, the highest the platform reaches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Make a small table
steps: The numbers climb to 10 at 90° and then fall back, so 90° is the peak.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the unit circle
steps: Sine is the HEIGHT UP of the point on the circle.
The highest point on any circle is straight up from the centre, and that direction is 90°.
